info.title: Screeps standalone server HTTP API
info.summary: Official Screeps World HTTP contract composed with the standalone compatibility profile
info.description: Operations a standalone single-world Screeps server provides for the official web client and community tools. Composed from the official Screeps World contract and the standalone compatibility profile; each operation's `x-profile` states whether it is an unchanged official operation (`required`), an official operation with documented standalone differences (`adapted`), a private-server protocol operation (`addition`) or a server-specific extension (`extension`). One world is served: `shard` values are accepted for official-client compatibility and ignored. Logical failures arrive as `{error}` usually with HTTP 200; never infer success from the status code.

get.description:
Returns the private profile of the account owning the token: id, username, e-mail (and an unconfirmed `emailDirty`), CPU, badge, GCL/power progress, credit balance (`money`), notification preferences, linked Steam/GitHub data, shard CPU limits (`cpuShard`, `cpuShardUpdatedTime`), account resources and power-creep experimentation state. Only fields present in storage are serialized. The official web client calls it after storing a token and keeps the result as the signed-in account; node-screeps-api resolves restricted tokens through `GET /api/user/name` + `GET /api/user/find` instead.

Standalone: Returns the private-server projection only (`_id`, `email`, `emailDirty`, `username`, `cpu`, `badge`, `password`, `lastRespawnDate`, `notifyPrefs`, `gcl`, `lastChargeTime`, `blocked`, `customBadge`, `power`, `money`, `steam`, `powerExperimentations`, `powerExperimentationTime`); never `cpuShard`, `cpuShardUpdatedTime`, `resources`, SSO links or legacy fields. `steam` is an empty object when no Steam account is linked. Token may be sent as `X-Token`, `Authorization: Bearer`, or `?token=`; each authenticated call issues a fresh token in the `X-Token` response header (default lifetime 60 s).

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

get.x-unverified: `blocked` and `customBadge` are neither read by the official web client nor typed by node-screeps-api; their presence on screeps.com is unverified. A non-null `restrictedAccessUntil` was not observed.

x-profile.reason: Standalone accounts carry Steam ownership as one boolean flag and profile-link visibility as a boolean, and `steam` is an empty object when no Steam account is linked (override: AuthSteamAccount).

post.description:
Exchanges an account e-mail address and password for a session token. The official web client posts `email`, `password`, its reCAPTCHA response (`recaptcha`) and, in the Steam desktop build, a hex-encoded Steam session ticket (`steamTicket`); it stores the returned `token` and then loads `GET /api/auth/me`.

Standalone: Primary authentication method of a standalone server. `email` accepts an e-mail address or a username (looked up case-insensitively unless it contains `@`); `recaptcha` and `steamTicket` are ignored. Passwords (8-1024 characters when set) are verified as scrypt hashes in constant time (unknown accounts still hash a dummy); every failure answers HTTP 401 `unauthorized`, and accounts without a configured password cannot sign in. Tokens are 64 lowercase hex characters, valid for `tokenLifetimeMs` (60 s default) and refreshed through the `X-Token` response header of authenticated calls.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope.

401.description: Invalid credentials. The official web client excludes sign-in from its HTTP 401 sign-out handling.

post.x-unverified: Only `token` is read from the success body; server-side handling of `recaptcha` and `steamTicket` and the logical error values are not evidenced.

post.summary: Sign in with a Steam session ticket
post.description:
Verifies a Steam session ticket from the Steam desktop build and returns a session token plus the authenticated SteamID, creating an account without a username the first time a SteamID signs in (the official web client then routes the player to username selection). With `useNativeAuth`, the ticket is a Greenworks encrypted app ticket instead of a session ticket.

Standalone: Authentication runs outside the world lock. Web API mode verifies tickets with Valve's AuthenticateUserTicket for app 464350 using an operator key. Opt-in native mode verifies encrypted app tickets with Greenworks and requires useNativeAuth to be true; platformVersion advertises the active mode. An unconfigured or mismatched scheme answers authentication method is not supported. Native mode retains the original published symmetric-key trust model and is not recommended for untrusted players. New accounts get 100 CPU, a default code branch and empty Memory.

200.description: Success, or a logical error in the HTTP 200 `{error}` envelope. Known `error` values: `authentication method is not supported`, `could not authenticate`, `invalid encrypted ticket`.

post.description:
Queues one account-level intent (market orders, deals, power creep management) for the next tick, as if issued by the caller's script. The official client uses it to issue `suicidePowerCreep` (`{id}`) from the power creep panel. The payload is wrapped in a one-element list and sanitized with the engine intent table; unknown names queue nothing but still succeed.

Standalone: Successive calls append to the caller's pending global intent lists, which the next tick merges into the caller's script intents. `generatePixel`, `unlockCpu` and `activateAccess` are dropped (only the player runtime may record them).

200.description: Intent queued. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.x-unverified: The official client issues only `suicidePowerCreep`; the accepted intent names and payload sanitization are inferred from the backend-local intent table. The success body beyond `ok` is not read.

post.summary: Queue a manual object or room intent
post.description:
Queues a manual intent for the next tick, executed as if issued by the caller's script (e.g. `suicide`, `unclaim`, `activateSafeMode`, `notifyWhenAttacked`, room-level `destroyStructure`/`removeConstructionSite`/`removeFlag`). The target room must exist, be a world room (`W…`/`E…`, otherwise `not supported`), and be inside the borders and open (`out of borders`). `activateSafeMode` is refused while any of the caller's controllers has active safe mode (`safe mode active already`). The payload is sanitized with the engine intent table (only schema fields kept; unknown names store `{}`), merged into the caller's queued manual intents for that target (`$merge`: objects deep-merge, arrays merge index by index), and the room is activated.

Standalone: Additionally requires `_id` (`invalid object`), requires the object to be in `room` (`invalid object`) and owned by the caller or, if unowned, in a room whose controller the caller owns (`not owner`), and rejects payload shapes the processor cannot handle (`invalid params`). An array `intent` is accepted only when `_id` is `room`; room-level list intents must be arrays of objects whose `roomName` equals `room`.

200.description: Intent queued. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `invalid room`, `not supported`, `out of borders`, `safe mode active already`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.description:
Recolors the caller's flag `name` in `room`. Both colors must be flag colors (`invalid params`). The official client sends the current `room` and `shard` with the flag name and both colors. The room's flag list is re-saved; an unknown name changes nothing but still succeeds.

Standalone: Without `room` nothing is saved and the call still succeeds; an empty flag document is created if the caller had none in that room. The success body is exactly `{ok: 1}`.

200.description: Flag colors saved. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `invalid params`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.x-unverified: Behavior without `room` is not evidenced for screeps.com (the official client always sends it; the community client omits it). The success body beyond `ok` is typed only by the community client.

200.description: Name is free. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `name exists`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

200.description: Name is free. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `invalid params`, `name exists`.

post.description:
Places a construction site for the caller without needing room visibility. Validation: coordinates 0..49, a `CONSTRUCTION_COST` structure type, name ≤ 50 characters and required for spawns (`invalid params`); The target room must exist, be a world room (`W…`/`E…`, otherwise `not supported`), and be inside the borders and open (`out of borders`). The spot must be valid (`invalid location`: not on the room edge, an extractor only on a mineral, not on a same-type structure/site or blocking structure (ramparts excepted), not on a wall (roads excepted), not next to an exit, and beside the edge only next to edge walls (roads/containers excepted)); the controller must not be owned/reserved by someone else (`not a controller owner`); the RCL must allow another structure of the type (`RCL not enough`); the caller must have fewer than 100 sites (`too many`). Mutation: inserts a `constructionSite` with progress 0 and `progressTotal` = construction cost (roads ×5 on swamp, ×150 on wall) and activates the room.

Standalone: The success body is `{ok: 1, _id}` without the MongoDB insert-result fields.

200.description: Site created. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `invalid params`, `invalid room`, `not supported`, `out of borders`, `invalid location`, `not a controller owner`, `RCL not enough`, `too many`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.x-unverified: The official client reads only `_id`; the MongoDB insert-result fields are typed only by the community client.

post.description:
Creates a flag, or moves the caller's flag with the same name, without needing room visibility. Validation: numeric `x`/`y` within 0..49, string `name` ≤ 60 characters, valid colors (`invalid params`); The target room must exist, be a world room (`W…`/`E…`, otherwise `not supported`), and be inside the borders and open (`out of borders`). Mutation: a flag with the same name is first removed from whichever room holds it and saved; then, if the caller already has `FLAGS_LIMIT` (10000) flags, the request fails with `flags limit exceeded` (the old flag stays removed); otherwise the flag is appended to the room's flag list (`name~color~secondaryColor~x~y`, `|`/`~` in names escaped).

Standalone: The success body is exactly `{ok: 1}` (no MongoDB `result`).

200.description: Flag saved. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `invalid params`, `invalid room`, `not supported`, `out of borders`, `flags limit exceeded`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.description:
Summons an NPC invader creep (user `2`, 1500 ticks to live, no loot) to test defenses in a room the caller owns or reserves. Refused when 5 invaders already exist in the room (`too many invaders exist`), when another player's creeps are present (`hostiles present`), when the controller is not owned/reserved by the caller (`not owned`). Any tile is accepted, walls included; the room is not activated. Mutation: inserts the creep with `userSummoned` set to the caller; body parts by `size`+`type`, boosted when `boosted` is truthy.

Standalone: An unknown `size`/`type` or a position outside 0..49 is rejected with `invalid params`.

200.description: Invader created. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `too many invaders exist`, `hostiles present`, `not owned`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.x-unverified: The official client does not read the success body; fields beyond `ok` are not evidenced for screeps.com.

x-profile.reason: The standalone success body carries the inserted invader creep document next to `ok`.

post.description:
Returns, for each requested room that exists, its status fields, controller ownership (`own`), sign, active safe mode, mineral (`minerals0`) and, for `<stat><interval>` stat names, the ranking of that statistic over the interval, plus the largest ranked value per stat (`statsMax`) and public profiles of every referenced user. screeps.com also returns, per room, `isPowerEnabled` for power-enabled controllers and the activated `decorations`, whose definitions come in the top-level `decorations`. Read-only. The official world map requests `owner0` below the closest zoom level and the selected layer stat (e.g. `energyHarvested8`) at the closest one, merges `stats` and `users` into its map state, sizes stat circles by `statsMax` and draws the room decorations.

Standalone: `rooms` must be an array and `statName` a string ending in digits (`invalid params` otherwise). Rankings are computed from per-minute statistics as arrays of `{user, value}` sorted descending; only users that still exist are counted. Non-string room names and rooms without a room document are ignored; `own.user` is omitted for an invader core without a user.

200.description: Map stats. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `invalid params`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.x-unverified: The per-stat ranking entry is documented only by the community client (one `{user, value}` object); the official client renders it in templates outside the analysed assets.

x-profile.reason: Standalone rankings for `<stat><interval>` are complete per-player arrays of `{user, value}` sorted descending instead of the single ranking entry documented for screeps.com.

post.description:
Starts playing: places the caller's first spawn at `x`,`y` in a free room. Preconditions: coordinates 0..49 and name ≤ 50 characters (`invalid params`), account not blocked (`blocked`), non-zero CPU (`no cpu`), at least 180 s since the last respawn (`too soon after last respawn`), playable room (The target room must exist, be a world room (`W…`/`E…`, otherwise `not supported`), and be inside the borders and open (`out of borders`). / `invalid room`), the caller owns no room objects (`already playing`), the controller exists (`invalid room`) and is unowned, unreserved and not bound to another user (`room busy`), and the tile is a valid construction spot (`invalid location`). Mutation: other players' creeps and construction sites in the room are removed, their structures become ruins (decaying after 100000 ticks), the level-0 controller is claimed at level 1 with 20000 ticks of safe mode, sources reset `invaderHarvested`, the spawn is inserted with 300 energy, the room's `invaderGoal` becomes 1000000, the room is activated, and the user's `active` counter becomes 10000. See `userWorldStatus` for the precondition state.

Placing the initial spawn of an account has been observed to reset the account's CPU allocation to the selected shard; callers must not assume a previously configured allocation (`userCpuShardsSet`, `POST /api/user/cpu-shards`) survives.

Standalone: Placing the first spawn does not change CPU settings.

200.description: Spawn placed. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `invalid params`, `blocked`, `no cpu`, `too soon after last respawn`, `invalid room`, `not supported`, `out of borders`, `already playing`, `room busy`, `invalid location`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.description:
Creates an unspawned power creep. Requires a free power level (GPL `floor((power / 1000) ^ (1/2))` minus one per existing creep and their levels; `not enough power level`), a valid class (`invalid class`) and a name unique among the caller's creeps (`name already exists`). Mutation: inserts the record at level 0 with 1000 max hits and 100 store capacity. The official client sends `{name, className}` from the creep editor.

Standalone: The success body is `{ok: 1, ...creep}`: a copy of the new record (`level: 0`, `hitsMax: 1000`, `storeCapacity: 100`, `spawnCooldownTime: 0`, `powers: {}`).

200.description: Created power creep. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `not enough power level`, `invalid class`, `name already exists`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.x-unverified: The official client does not read the success body; fields beyond `ok` are not evidenced for screeps.com.

x-profile.reason: The standalone success body carries a copy of the created power creep record next to `ok`.

post.description: Deletes one of the caller's unspawned power creeps (`invalid id`, `spawned`, `already being deleted`). Mutation: during power experimentation the record is removed immediately; otherwise `deleteTime` is set to now + `POWER_CREEP_DELETE_COOLDOWN` (24 h) and the engine deletes it then. The official client sends `{id}` (refusing locally while the creep is spawned) and reloads the list afterwards.

post.description: Spends one of the caller's power experimentation resets (`no power resets` when none are left) to start a 24-hour window in which power creep deletion is immediate. post.description:
Sets the complete power levels of one of the caller's power creeps; the new creep level is the sum of power levels. Refusals: `invalid id`, `invalid powers` (not an object), `invalid power <id>`, `invalid class for power <id>`, `invalid value for power <id>` (not a number), `cannot downgrade power <id>`, `invalid max value for power <id>` (> 5), `max level` (> 25), `not enough level for power <id>`, `powers set is not valid` (levels not reachable in requirement order), `not enough power level` (insufficient free GPL). Mutation: merges `{level}` into each non-zero power (keeping cooldowns) and sets `level`, `hitsMax = 1000 × (level + 1)` and `storeCapacity = 100 × (level + 1)` on the record and, when spawned, on its room object. The official client sends `{id, powers}` with the complete level per power id.

Standalone: Non-integer levels are also rejected with `invalid value for power <id>`.

200.description: Upgrade applied. Logical failures are reported with HTTP 200 and `{error}`: `invalid id`, `invalid powers`, `invalid power <id>`, `invalid class for power <id>`, `invalid value for power <id>`, `cannot downgrade power <id>`, `invalid max value for power <id>`, `max level`, `not enough level for power <id>`, `powers set is not valid`, `not enough power level`.

X-Token.description: Rotated session token when issued by the server; store it for subsequent authenticated requests.

post.summary: Toggle attack notifications for an object
post.description:
